initial_plan.can_answer: yes: crash-record totals can describe the distribution across weekdays, but do not measure risk or account for differing numbers of each weekday in the calendar period
initial_plan.denominator: none; each row is one reported crash
initial_plan.population: crash records with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive
initial_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday

data_check.facts: check_1.csv: 2,132,218 eligible records; each target year has observed dates from January 1 through December 31; zero source rows have NULL crash_date; zero rows use the checked sentinel dates; weekday is derivable for all eligible rows.
data_check.meaning_and_decisions: The date filter excludes no rows for a missing date within the target period; rows outside 2013-2025 are not in the planned population. All eligible rows are kept. crash_date is a DATE, so empty strings, unknown words, and impossible dates are not representable. No rows are reclassified or counted differently.

final_plan.can_answer: yes, as a distribution of police-reported crash records by weekday
final_plan.denominator: none; each row is one reported crash
final_plan.population: all crash records with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive
final_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
final_plan.limitations: The data check found no missing crash dates and full-year observed date endpoints in every target year. This is a count of reported crashes, not a traffic-exposure-adjusted risk measure; pooled totals also reflect the number of calendar occurrences of each weekday.
